rounds.text: ITC offers an exceptionally efficient operation trading at a discount, evidenced by a P/E of 17.35x against a sector benchmark of 19.04x [E6] and a market-leading ROA of 21.52% compared to the sector benchmark of 3.54% [E8]. Shareholders benefit from immediate cash returns through a robust dividend yield of 5.21% [E4]. Operational momentum is expanding as earnings growth is accelerating [E66] with sales growing QoQ [E65], resulting in a scenario where recent profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 31% [E57]. The company is actively investing in future capacity, reflected in a 46.8% increase in CWIP to Rs 1602 Cr for Mar 2026 [E41]. Conceded: top-line momentum has faced recent headwinds, as trailing twelve months sales growth stands at -3% [E17] and YoY sales declined -11% [E70], leaving the stock sitting at just 2% of its 52-week range [E5]. Nevertheless, given its vastly superior asset returns [E8] and capex build-up underway [E41], the market is under-appreciating a business whose fundamental profit growth is outperforming price expectations [E57].

ITC's top-line momentum shows a clear downward trajectory, with 3-year compounded sales growth slowing to 4% [E16], trailing twelve-month sales contracting by -3% [E17], and YoY sales declining by 11% [E70]. Despite this top-line deceleration, the stock commands an elevated valuation relative to its balance sheet assets, carrying a P/B of 4.83x compared to the sector benchmark of 1.82x [E7]. Market sentiment reflects these operational headwinds, leaving the share price sitting at just 2% of its 52-week trading range [E5]. Conceded: ITC maintains strong underlying profitability with an ROA of 21.52% versus the sector's 3.54% [E8], delivers a generous dividend yield of 5.21% [E4], and trades at a slight P/E discount of 17.35x compared to the sector benchmark of 19.04x [E6].

While we concede that 3-year compounded sales growth has slowed to 4% [E16], trailing twelve-month sales contracted by -3% [E17], and YoY sales declined by 11% [E70], the business is already demonstrating a fundamental turnaround with sales up QoQ [E65] and accelerating earnings growth [E66]. This operational pivot is further supported by a 46.8% increase in capital work-in-progress to Rs 1602 Cr, signaling a major growth spend and capex build-up phase underway [E41]. We also concede that the company's P/B of 4.83x [E7] (or 4.80x based on a price of ₹ 278 and book value of ₹ 57.9 [E2]) exceeds the sector benchmark of 1.82x [E7]. However, this premium is entirely justified by ITC's superior capital efficiency, boasting an ROA of 21.52% compared to the sector benchmark of just 3.54% [E8]. Finally, while the stock sitting at 2% of its 52-week range [E5] reflects depressed sentiment, it has created a highly attractive valuation gap where the company trades at a discounted P/E of 17.35x [E6] (or 17.6x [E1]) against a sector benchmark of 19.04x [E6], all while yielding a strong 5.21% dividend [E4] and outperforming expectations as profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 31% [E57].

Conceded: ITC yields a strong dividend of 5.21% [E4], delivers a superior ROA of 21.52% compared to the sector benchmark of 3.54% [E8], and trades at a modest P/E discount of 17.35x [E6] (or 17.6x [E1]) versus the sector benchmark of 19.04x [E6]. However, the bull's turnaround narrative built on sequential QoQ sales gains [E65], accelerating earnings growth [E66], and CWIP expanding 46.8% to Rs 1602 Cr [E41] fails to offset the immediate reality of trailing twelve-month sales contracting by -3% [E17] and YoY sales dropping -11% [E70]. Top-line sluggishness is a multi-year issue, as 3-year compounded sales growth sits at just 4% [E16] with poor 5-year growth flagged at 9.87% [E63], while both 10-year (7%) [E14] and 5-year (10%) [E15] compounded growth lag the sector median sales growth of 12.7% [E76]. In light of this persistent top-line drag, demanding a heavy P/B premium of 4.83x [E7] (or 4.80x based on a price of ₹ 278 and book value of ₹ 57.9 [E2]) against the sector benchmark of 1.82x [E7] is unjustifiable for a business experiencing negative TTM revenue growth [E17].
